- [FACT] User inquired about the specifics of a Boeing 717.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Boeing 717 is a twin-engine, single-aisle regional jet aircraft originally developed by McDonnell Douglas prior to its acquisition by Boeing in 1997.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Boeing 717 has a seating capacity of up to 117 passengers, depending on the configuration chosen by the airline.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Length of the Boeing 717: 37.8 meters (124 feet 1 inch).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wingspan of the Boeing 717: 28.5 meters (93 feet 6 inches).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Height of the Boeing 717: 8.9 meters (29 feet 2 inches).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Maximum takeoff weight of the Boeing 717: 53,800 kilograms (118,500 pounds).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Range of the Boeing 717: 2,060 to 3,675 kilometers (1,280 to 2,280 miles).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Cruise speed of the Boeing 717: 828 kilometers per hour (515 miles per hour).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Boeing 717 is powered by two Rolls-Royce BR715 turbofans, each producing 18,500 pounds of thrust.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Boeing 717 has a modern glass cockpit with advanced avionics, including a flight management system, electronic flight instrument displays, and a digital autopilot.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Boeing 717 is known for its fuel efficiency and low noise emissions.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Boeing 717 is typically used for short to medium-haul flights and is popular among regional airlines and low-cost carriers.
